steps.title: Subtle and textured
steps.body: Sémillon gives medium to full-bodied whites with lemon, lanolin, beeswax, grass and, with age, honey, toast and nuts. Acidity is low to medium, texture waxy and oily. Young, it can seem neutral; its strength is texture and ageing. It's Bordeaux's most planted white grape.

steps.title: Thin skins
steps.body: Sémillon's thin, golden skins make it prone to rot, including noble rot, Botrytis cinerea. That's a weakness in wet years but a gift for sweet wine. It's vigorous and productive. In Bordeaux it's often blended with Sauvignon Blanc, which adds acidity and aroma to Sémillon's body.
steps.highlight: Thin skins, prone to noble rot

steps.prompt: Why is Sémillon so suited to noble rot?
steps.explanation: Thin skins let Botrytis cinerea attack easily.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for pale to medium lemon colour, a subtle nose of lemon, lanolin and sometimes grass, and a waxy, round palate. In blends with Sauvignon, Sémillon adds weight and texture. Aged Sémillon is unmistakable: toast, honey and lemon curd, even without oak.
